_comment: Corrections applied on top of the raw database exports in this folder.
The *_Unified_PIDs.json files are left exactly as the Tata databases have them,
so it stays clear what came from Tata and what came from us. Anything generated
for downstream use - the CarScanner profiles, the markdown reference - applies
this overlay. Every entry states its evidence. See ../CORRECTIONS.md.

BMS:347D.why: same DB lists $347E as both W and kW; 0.1 W/bit cannot represent a 105 kW pack in 2 bytes, 0.1 kW/bit can

BMS:347E.why: the DB carries two rows for this DID, one W one kW; kW is the consistent reading

BMS:347F.why: already correct - listed for completeness of the power group

VECU:35B0.why: the BMS defines the identical signal at $353E as Ah; this is charge throughput, not a temperature

VECU:35B1.why: the BMS defines the identical signal at $353F as Ah

BMS:3492.why: BMS Power Supply voltage, resolution 0.001 - raw is millivolts

VECU:3428.issue: 1-byte charging current limit carrying a 40 offset, which is the coolant-temperature scaling pattern
VECU:3428.advice: prefer $352F 'Charging current limit requested by VCU', 2 bytes at resolution 0.1 with no offset - same signal, sane scaling

BMS:3497.issue: offset 50 where $3410 and $3411 and every other coolant temperature in every Tata database use 40
BMS:3497.advice: verify against $3410 on the car; if it reads 10 C high, the offset is 40

BMS:3481.issue: TDS 20.0 says resolution 1 in mV; TDS 8.9S said 0.1 in V - a factor of 100
BMS:3481.advice: TDS 20.0 is preferred. The negative busbar sits near chassis potential, so a millivolt scale is physically sensible where a 0.1 V scale is not
